business_scope.primary_industry_name: Product Interface Design and Digital Design Subscription Agency

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU BIT network: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union investment protection agreements with third states
EU external agreements: Trade and investment provisions in EU Free Trade Agreements (e.g., EU-Japan, EU-Canada CETA, EU-Vietnam)
Double Tax Treaties: Luxembourg DTA network with 90+ jurisdictions (e.g., US, France, Germany, Netherlands, UK)
Multilateral: Energy Charter Treaty (in review), Hague Convention on Apostille, ICSID Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, incl. Law of 27 September 2018 and Law of 25 June 2020); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and its implementing Grand-Ducal Regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register Extract for corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or authorized corporate registrar in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for apostille-contracting states) OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of valid government-issued passport or national ID for each UBO (natural person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent issuing authority / notary public in the UBO's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; notarization sufficient for EU/EEA passports

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or credit institution in the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized translation into French/German/Luxembourgish; notarial seal (apostille not usually required unless specified by the RBE/AML compliance policy)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Luxembourg service provider / designated manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate board of shareholders or individual UBO executed before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague signatory states)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, partners, authorized signatories and counterparties against Luxembourg's national AML/CFT lists, UN consolidated financial sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, US OFAC (SDN list and sectors, for USD transactions), UK HMT (where relevant), and FATF Public Statements. PEPs are assessed in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12 and CSSF Circular 18/698; enhanced due diligence applies to foreign PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions. Screening is performed at client acceptance, periodically thereafter, and upon any trigger event, with complete documentation retained in the compliance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés via e-Recours; https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official filing languages: French, German, Luxembourgish. Names must not be misleading and must be expressed in Latin script; non-Latin scripts require an approved Latin transliteration. The legal designation 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale' must be clearly appended to the chosen name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS refuses a name on grounds of identity, confusion or public policy, the applicant may: (1) submit an amended name via the responsible notary or authorized e-filing agent within 5 business days; (2) file a reasoned administrative complaint with the Registrar for formal reconsideration; (3) appeal to the Tribunal administratif within one month of a final administrative refusal. Extension of the 30-day reservation window is not generally available; a fresh name search and reservation is required after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office is not permissible. The SCSp must maintain a genuine registered office in Luxembourg where official notices can be physically served. Domiciliation by an approved registered agent (licensed professional of the financial sector or authorized domiciliation undertaking) is accepted for a subscription-driven UI/UX design agency, provided the address is a physical office location and the agent accepts formal service of process on behalf of the partnership.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) and corporate/AML structuring advice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (avocat à la Cour) engaged by the partners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly rate for cross-border partnership work (approximately EUR 450-800 per hour); fixed or capped fee per scope of engagement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved domiciliation agent / professional of the financial sector (PFS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Customary annual domiciliation tariff for low-risk commercial partnerships (approximately EUR 1,200 - 1,800)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance certificate (certificat de non-collision / name availability search)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Grand-Ducal Regulation on RCS fees (EUR 20-60 per search/extract)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and consular legalization of UBO documents (passports, incumbency certificates, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, consulate/chamber of commerce, apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee scale and consular charges; varies by jurisdiction (Hague Apostille vs. Consular Legalization)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT pre-incorporation due diligence (PEP, sanctions, UBO verification and risk file setup)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market standard flat fee for AML KYC file set-up and PEP/sanctions screening under CSSF rules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) and Ministry of Justice (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed registration fee (approximately EUR 75-150) plus RESA publication tariff (EUR 25-40)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, particularly Articles 1, 10, 27–28, 41–42 and 155–159 concerning partnerships; the Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and Receuil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA); and the Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 72a Avenue des Hauts-Fourneaux, L-4362 Esch-sur-Alzette, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; online filing portal at www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / Contrat de société (deed of constitution and partnership agreement of the SCSp), executed either as a notarial deed or as a private writing, filed with the RCS together with the statutory RCS registration form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SCSp; the partnership agreement fixes the contributions freely. No escrow or blocked bank account is legally required. Contributions may be in cash, in kind (valued per the deed), or in industry, but industry contributions are reserved to the general partner. If a notarial deed references cash contributions, the notary may require a bank confirmation of deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company approve, adopt, and execute the deed of constitution and the partnership agreement of the SCSp (the 'Partnership'), and that the Company, acting as general partner, subscribe to its contribution therein; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Partnership be fixed at [●], Luxembourg, and that the RCS registration and RESA publication filings be lodged with the Luxembourg Business Registers; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed managing director/representative, and [Name] be appointed compliance officer, each with full authority to open bank accounts, appoint service providers, and perform all acts necessary to operationalize the Partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Deed of Constitution (Contrat de Société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public appointed by the partners, or directly the general partner where a private writing is selected; ultimate supervision by the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement containing the general partner and limited partners, their contributions, profit-sharing rules, management powers, termination terms, and the Luxembourg registered office address. Cause the deed to be executed by all partners. A notarial deed is elective for a pure service SCSp but is recommended for legal comfort; it becomes mandatory if the SCSp acquires Luxembourg real estate or elects legal personality. Where the general partner is a corporate entity, produce its board resolution authorising the formation and its current corporate extracts.
required_dossiers: Full legal names, dates of birth, and addresses of all general and limited partners
Draft partnership agreement / deed of constitution (Contrat de société)
Corporate documents of the general partner (articles of association, resolution of its governing body, certificate of good standing or non-inscription)
Proof of address or lease agreement evidencing the intended registered office in Luxembourg
Bank confirmation letter for any cash contribution if a notarial deed is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or RCS queries missing partner details or insufficient corporate authority of the general partner, supplement the dossier with re-executed resolutions, apostilled or certified corporate extracts, corrected identity documents, and, if necessary, draft an addendum to the partnership agreement and re-execute before the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Department, electronic filing portal www.lbr.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the LBR e-filing platform and file the constitutive deed together with the standard RCS incorporation form. Disclose the legal form (SCSp), the registered office, the duration (fixed or indefinite), the identities of the general partner and authorised managers, and the RCS number of any corporate general partner. Pay the electronic filing fee. The RCS verifies legal compliance and issues the RCS registration number.
required_dossiers: Signed deed of constitution (Contrat de société) in PDF
Completed RCS registration form (form for incorporation of a commercial company)
Identity documents of all partners and appointed managers
Registered office address confirmation (lease or title deed)
Written power of attorney if the filing is lodged through a third-party representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or a formal refusal (mise en demeure), correct the flagged defects, such as missing signatures, incomplete manager identification, or contradictory capital clauses, amend the deed where necessary, and resubmit within the one-month appeal window. The LBR helpdesk may accept minor corrections without requiring a fresh deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the registration extract is transmitted to RESA for publication. Review the published notice to confirm the accurate display of the RCS number, legal form, registered office, general partner, and managers. If publication is not triggered automatically, file an explicit publication request through the LBR portal and settle the applicable publication fee.
required_dossiers: Reservation or receipt for the RESA publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any typographical or legal discrepancy in the RESA notice by lodging a corrective declaration with the RCS and requesting a supplementary publication. Erroneous third-party reliance is mitigated once the corrected version is published.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Ultimate Beneficial Owners in the Register (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), operated under the Ministry of Justice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file with the RBE the identity of any natural persons who directly or indirectly own or control the SCSp, including through partnership interests or voting control over the general partner. Submit the RBE filing online via the LBR portal, attaching proof of identity and a corporate structure chart. Obtain the RBE access credentials to be retained by the general partner and the compliance officer for statutory updates.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card copies of every ultimate beneficial owner
Declaration specifying the nature and percentage of ownership or control
Corporate structure chart identifying any intermediate entities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE rejects the filing for incomplete documentation, correct the beneficial ownership description, provide an updated structure chart, or, where no natural-person UBO can be identified, file the statutory declaration of non-ascertainment with justification. Late filings are subject to criminal fines and daily penalties; voluntary correction minimises exposure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, Direct Tax, and Social Security Registration (as applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, file the VAT form (Formulaire n° 1) with the AED where the SCSp anticipates taxable design subscription services in Luxembourg or intends to make periodic VAT returns. Register as an employer with the CCSS if staff will be engaged. Direct corporate income tax registration is normally effected automatically through the RCS-AED/ACD data exchange; confirm the assigned business registration number for all official correspondence.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract and RCS number
VAT registration form (Formulaire n° 1) signed by the authorised manager
Identification of the appointed manager or representative
Payroll and employment declarations where staff will be recruited (for CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AED queries the place of supply or the nature of the activities, submit a cover letter describing the UI-UX design subscription model and the customer base, together with a sample contract. A late VAT registration may give rise to administrative fines up to EUR 250, which can be mitigated by filing a voluntary disclosure and demonstrating good faith; take advice before the first invoice is issued to cross-border clients.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 7410 (UI/UX product design and design subscription services). No Luxembourg industrial or commercial establishment authorisation is required for office-based design-only activities following the abolition of the general establishment authorisation regime by the Law of 16 June 2017. If manufacturing were undertaken, the competent authority would be the Ministry of the Economy – Department of Industry and Competitiveness.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required. No industrial exploitation permit (autorisation d’exploitation / Kommissionserlaabnes) applies to non-industrial office-based design and subscription activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l’environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency), 1 Avenue du Rock’n’Roll, L-4361 Esch-sur-Alzette.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 'no EIA required'. The Luxembourg Law of 22 May 2008 on Environmental Impact Assessment and its annexes do not list software design, IT consultancy, or digital subscription offices among projects requiring an EIA notice, registration, or full impact study.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial process discharge. The SCSp must nevertheless dispose of electrical and electronic office equipment in accordance with the WEEE Directive transposition (Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 March 2015) and use approved waste collectors; general office wastewater discharge must comply with the municipal sewer bylaws; no VOC process emission thresholds arise from UI-UX design activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: the leased office premises must have a valid occupancy permit, and any common areas open to the public require a fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the Corps grand-ducal d’incendie et de secours. Structural load: the lessor must confirm that the premises support normal office floor loading; no special structural certification is required for IT workstations. Occupational clearance: the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) requires compliance with the Labour Code on work organisation, VDU ergonomics, electrical equipment safety checks, fire-escape signage, and a written risk assessment (évaluation des risques) prepared by the employer and kept on site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg direct tax administration: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), 45 boulevard Roosevelt, L-2982 Luxembourg; indirect tax administration: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT). Central e-filing and clearance portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu (Acajou engine). Commercial registration: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS, Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Assess VAT nexus - B2B UI/UX design subscriptions to EU customers are reverse-charged in the customer's Member State and require an LU VAT number plus EC Sales Lists; B2C digital subscriptions to consumers in other EU states may be declared via OSS with an LU VAT number; pure non-EU B2B/B2C export services create no mandatory registration. Step 2: A non-EU partner/entity acting as SCSp must appoint an AEDT-approved VAT representative in Luxembourg before filing. Step 3: Apply for VAT registration via MyGuichet.lu (AEDT 'demande d'immatriculation à la TVA') attaching the RCS extract of the SCSp, partnership agreement, identity documents, power of attorney, and expected turnover. Step 4: Obtain the national 11-digit matricule d'identification (TIN) from ACD and the separate LU + 8-digit VAT number from AEDT. Step 5: Register as employer (payroll withholding) with ACD and with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) if any personnel are engaged. No CIT registration is required for the SCSp because it is fiscally transparent and not a corporate income tax subject.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - the SCSp (introduced by law of 12 July 2013 amending the law of 10 August 1915, art. 65-1) is a special limited partnership that is statutorily fiscally neutral/transparent; it has no legal personality (unless a specific election is made under commercial law), is not subject to Luxembourg CIT or municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and its profits are allocated and taxed directly at partner level according to each partner's participation and personal tax profile.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or classification election exists under Luxembourg domestic tax law; pass-through status attaches by statutory form. The partnership agreement may nevertheless allocate rights, profits and losses in accordance with economic substance, subject to Luxembourg arm's-length and substance rules (art. 8 Abgabenordnung). A US partner may file a US check-the-box election (disregarded entity) for US purposes, which Luxembourg ignores for CIT. Luxembourg applies the ATAD 2 hybrid mismatch rules (LIR articles 168ter to 168septies, effective from 1 January 2020) to neutralise any double non-taxation arising from divergent foreign classifications of the SCSp.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA) under the amended Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 (loi concernant la TVA - VLDT), aligned with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC and administered by the AEDT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 - domestic small-business franchise (art. 57 VLDT) for established small suppliers only; NOT available to non-EU established SCSp. Non-EU SCSp supplying B2C electronically supplied design subscriptions must VAT register in Luxembourg or use the Union OSS/IOSS scheme from the first euro of sales. EU-established SCSp may benefit from the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold for intra-EU B2C distance sales/digital services (OSS). B2B design services to taxable customers in other EU Member States always trigger reverse-charge handling and require an LU VAT number, with no local threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, electronic stamping, or continuous transaction control regime is operative in Luxembourg. E-invoicing is permitted but not mandatory for B2B; where used, the vendor must ensure authenticity of origin and integrity of content (qualified e-signature, EDI, or equivalent controls, art. 12 VLDT). Mandatory electronic filing applies to VAT returns (monthly/quarterly) and EC Sales Lists via MyGuichet.lu. Taxpayers must produce a standardised electronic accounting file (fichier d'écritures comptables normalisé, FeC/XML) upon tax audit. EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) may introduce harmonised e-invoicing and digital reporting by 2030.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT under art. 41 VLDT where the goods are physically exported outside the EU, evidenced by a released Single Administrative Document (SAD, status A). Services: B2B UI/UX design and subscription services supplied by the LU SCSp to a customer established outside the EU are governed by the Business-to-Business place-of-supply rule (art. 44 of Directive 2006/112/EC) and are therefore located outside Luxembourg - reportable in the VAT return as exempt-with-credit at 0% with documented proof of the customer's non-EU status; B2C automated/electronic design subscription products supplied to non-EU consumers are likewise outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (no registration or reporting duty in Luxembourg). B2B supplies to EU established customers are not zero-rated but reverse-charged at the customer's VAT number.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document - SAD with release status A)
Commercial invoice (reference to the subscription agreement, OSS/ECSL cross-reference and VAT exemption clause)
Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB) or CMR multimodal transport document evidencing physical dispatch from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 payment evidence from the non-EU customer
Proof of non-EU customer status (VIES negative validation or foreign tax/residence certificate)
Service delivery evidence (signed statement of work, acceptance certificates, usage/task logs for the design-as-a-service subscription)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess VAT for up to five years, with the limitation period suspended in cases of fraud. Improper zero-rating or missing export documentation triggers reassessment at the standard 17% VAT plus statutory late-payment interest of 0.6% per month (7.2% p.a.), and administrative fines under art. 73 VLDT ranging from EUR 250 to EUR 10,000 per non-compliant document or invoice. Fraudulent misuse of the zero-rating/export regime (false export declarations, fictitious non-EU customers) constitutes tax evasion under art. 80 of the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), punished by fines up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years, possible publication of the conviction, joint and several liability of the general partner (gérant) and managing partners, disqualification of directors, and full clawback of input VAT deducted in connection with the disallowed transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the national monetary and statistical authority; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises licensed banks and payment/EMI institutions. Exchange controls were abolished in Luxembourg under EU capital-movement liberalization (Article 63 TFEU) and national rules; no ex-ante authorization from the BCL or CSSF is required for cross-border capital flows, trade settlement, or repatriation by non-residents.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both the current account and the capital account. Luxembourg imposes no exchange-control authorization, no quantitative limits, and no central-bank pre-approval on cross-border payments. For an SCSp, which is fiscally transparent, current-account profit remittances to partners face no Luxembourg withholding tax; the real practical hurdle is purely bank-level source-of-funds and ultimate-beneficial-owner verification. The SCSp may hold multi-currency accounts, invoice in EUR or foreign currency, and freely convert balances. The only compliance perimeter is BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting and CSSF AML/KYC enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg law and CSSF guidance impose no mandatory timeframe, no conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export or service-trade receipts. The design-subscription agency may retain foreign currency indefinitely, convert at commercial bank rates, or use the proceeds directly for outbound vendor payments. The sole statutory duty is ancillary: transactions with non-resident counterparties exceeding EUR 12,500 per month must be declared to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistics, without restricting the transaction itself.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, société anonyme (BIL)
Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkees)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-High for ancillary payment flows, Low as a sole treasury backbone. EU/EEA electronic-money institutions (Wise Europe SA, Revolut) can passport payment and EMI services into Luxembourg under PSD2 via CSSF notification and typically provide EUR IBANs, low-cost cross-currency conversion, and high-velocity API settlement — operationally well suited to Stripe Billing subscription sweeps. However, most EMIs apply enhanced scrutiny to partnerships registered as SCSp because the entity lacks separate legal personality; the account must be opened by the general partner (gérant) for the account of the SCSp. EMIs also cannot provide committed credit, commercial LC, or substantive treasury FX lines. The recommended blueprint places a tier-1 Luxembourg bank account as the ultimate treasury anchor, with Wise serving as a collection/disbursement rail that sweeps net proceeds into the primary bank account, and Stripe Billing retained as the merchant-of-record for recurring design subscriptions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is the default expectation, but CSSF-compliant video identification is increasingly accepted for low-risk corporate clients. The banks will require at least one interview with a natural person — the general partner if an individual, or a senior managing director/authorized signatory of the corporate GP — together with production of the executed partnership agreement, the corporate GP's board resolution, and passport/identification documents. Fully remote opening is possible only where the corporate GP is an existing long-term client of the bank, or where the bank uses biometric video-identification with notarized electronic signatures in line with CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004, as amended. Since the SCSp has no legal personality, every credit mandate, signature card, and instructions contract must be executed by the general partner expressly acting on behalf of the SCSp, and the bank will typically also request a legal-opinion comfort letter confirming the authority of the GP to bind the partnership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp lacking legal personality and perceived as an unregulated collective-investment structure despite carrying an active operating business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed partnership agreement dated by all partners; corporate resolution of the general partner; Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE) extract; a notarized or lawyer-certified legal opinion under the Luxembourg Law of 12 July 2013 confirming the SCSp is a commercial partnership without legal personality, not a regulated fund; a business plan evidencing genuine UI/UX subscription operations under ISIC 7410.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fiscally transparent pass-through classification triggering look-through KYC on every partner and heightened source-of-wealth requests
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO ownership diagram; source-of-wealth statement and bank references for every natural person holding more than 25% capital or control; incorporation extracts and registry filings for each intermediate corporate partner; tax-transparency confirmation from a Luxembourg practicing accountant; capital-account ledger of the SCSp showing subscribed and paid-in amounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity recurring subscription revenue from many dispersed online payers via Stripe and Wise, resembling money-service-business or merchant-aggregator flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe Billing settlement reports showing merchant-of-record logic and platform payout archive; Wise transaction statements; executed subscription agreements and live dashboard extract connecting each receivable to the identified subscriber; sample invoices and the agency's published standard terms; annual revenue forecast broken down by client jurisdiction to demonstrate predictable low-value B2B/B2C flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to non-EU design contractors triggering enhanced due diligence, sanctions screening, and tax-evasion red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC pack containing passport or commercial-registry extract, executed service agreement, pricing schedule and invoice-supporting deliverables; sanctions-screening output from an independent screening tool; where the counterparty is US-connected, a Form W-8BEN-E or equivalent OECD tax form; a commercial-rationale memorandum for service routing through each relevant jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident majority ownership with planned profit withdrawals, raising shell-structuring and round-tripping concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial-substance file: Luxembourg office lease or co-working agreement; payroll or external-PEO evidence of locally engaged staff; UI/UX project pipeline and client communications; Luxembourg corporate tax and VAT registration numbers (matricule and TVA); arm's-length pricing documentation and capital-account ledgers demonstrating economic activity in Luxembourg.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital contributions are routed via SEPA Credit Transfer to the SCSp's IBAN for EUR, or via SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR/non-SEPA remittances. The wire narrative must contain the SCSp registered name, the Luxembourg matricule, the capital-call reference, and the purpose narrative 'equity contribution to partnership capital'. No central-bank permit or exchange-control approval is required. If the contributing partner is non-resident and the monthly aggregate exceeds EUR 12,500, the BCL balance-of-payments direct-investment declaration applies and must be filed by the resident recipient (the SCSp or its appointed filing agent). Best practice is to open a dedicated capital-contribution sub-account at the tier-1 bank to maintain an untainted audit trail distinct from operating subscription revenue; the contribution is then posted to the partners' capital accounts and evidenced by signed capital-call notices.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating disbursements — designer contractor fees, SaaS license fees, cloud infrastructure, and subcontractor royalties — settle via SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant for EUR, and via SWIFT MT103 for USD, GBP, and other non-EUR payments. Commercial letters of credit are structurally unsuitable for service exports and should not be used; payment against invoice is the standard. USD proceeds collected through Stripe and Wise are swept into the SCSp's tier-1 Luxembourg bank account and converted to EUR through the treasury FX line. Vendor payments above EUR 50,000, or any payment touching a high-risk or exposed jurisdiction, should be sent as ISO 20022 pain.001/pain.002 messages with structured remittance data, pre-validation of beneficiary BIC, and prior OFAC/EU-sanctions screening. To minimize exception handling, the agency should maintain a static vendor master with pre-validated banking data and invoice-level reconciliation files.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD and EUR/GBP foreign-exchange forwards (fixed-date contracts) with a licensed Luxembourg/EU bank under ISDA 2002 or a short-form FX Annex, used to lock net USD subscription receivables for up to 12 months
Foreign-exchange swaps for rolling conversion of daily USD sweeps while matching forward cover maturity to eliminate open overnight currency exposure
Cross-currency swaps for medium-term alignment of multi-year USD-denominated design-retainer revenue against EUR operating costs
Vanilla European currency options purchased from a top-tier counterparty to protect downside on material non-EUR receivables while preserving upside participation

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted-currency jurisdictions (CNH, INR, KRW, BRL) solely to hedge settlement exposure where the agency has paying clients in countries with non-deliverable local currencies
Overnight/forward EUR and USD deposits combined with balance-sheet netting of USD subscription receivables against USD vendor payables to structurally reduce external conversion volumes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RBE annual confirmation (annual confirmation of registered beneficial owners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for calendar-year SCSp; non-calendar-year SCSp must confirm within one month after the ordinary partners' meeting and in any event no later than eight months after year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or materially incorrect RBE information exposes the general partner and responsible managers to criminal fines of EUR 250 to EUR 125,000 and imprisonment from one month to five years; the RBE may also initiate administrative compliance measures and public prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (depôt des comptes annuels) – conditional on applicability thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of accounts by the partners and by 31 July of the following year for calendar-year SCSp; where the SCSp qualifies for the statutory exemption, no filing is made.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may trigger court-ordered compliance, fines of EUR 100 to EUR 10,000, and for repeated non-compliance, administrative strike-off or judicial dissolution proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory for a Luxembourg SCSp because it has no legal personality and at least one general partner has unlimited liability; a mandatory independent audit arises only if the SCSp is a regulated AIF/AIFM, or if all general partners are limited-liability entities and the partnership exceeds two of three criteria: total balance sheet EUR 4.4m, net turnover EUR 8.8m, average employees 50 for two consecutive years.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as derived from the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies and applicable accounting legislation; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for voluntary consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: In every calendar year, the SCSp must electronically confirm the accuracy of the RBE entries; any transfer or acquisition of partnership interests must be filed with the RBE within 30 days; the general partner designates an authorized filer and maintains partner declarations evidencing changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp entity level (fiscally transparent); Luxembourg corporate partners are taxed on allocated shares at the aggregate Luxembourg City rate of 22.80% (15% IRC + 1.05% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Pass-through: no CIT, MBT or NWT is levied on the SCSp itself. Corporate partners can benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption on allocated dividends (100% exemption) and the 80% IP box deduction on qualifying design IP income; capital gains on SCSp interests held for >12 months may qualify for the participation exemption. No VAT on deemed exports if EU reverse charge applies.
